weeks.title: Q1: W1 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison using “ten times as many as.”
sc: I can describe the relationship of “ten times as many as” for tens and ones.
I can describe the relationship of “ten times as many as” for hundreds and tens.
I can describe the relationship of “ten times as many as” for thousands and hundreds.
I can model each relationship of “ten times as many as” using a place value chart.
I can write an equation to represent the model on the place value chart.

days.lo: I am learning that a digit represents 10 times the value of the digit to its right.
sc: I can multiply single units by 10 to build a place value chart to 1 million and divide by 10 to reverse the process.
I can multiply multiple copies of one unit by 10.
I can divide multiple copies of one unit by 10.
I can multiply and divide copies of two different units by 10

days.lo: I am learning to name numbers within 1 billion by building an understanding of the place value chart and placement of commas.
sc: I can recognize patterns in the base ten system.
I can place commas and name the numbers.
I can add to make 10 of a unit and bundle up to 1 billion.
I can multiply 10 times as many with multiple units.

days.lo: I am learning to read and write multi-digit numbers using base ten numerals, number names, and expanded form.
sc: I can write a five-digit number in word form and expanded notation
I can write a number in standard and expanded notation when given a number in word form.
I can convert a number in expanded notation to word and standard form.
I can label to represent numbers on the place value chart.

weeks.title: Q1: W2 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to compare numbers based on meanings of the digits and using <, >, = to show the comparison.
sc: I can compare two numbers.
I can compare two numbers with an equal amount of the largest unit.
I can compare the values of multiple numbers using a place value chart.
I can compare numbers in different number forms.

days.lo: I am learning to find 1, 10, and 100 thousand and 1, 10, and 100 million more and less than a given number.
sc: I can find 1 thousand more and 1 thousand less than a given number.
I can find 10 thousand more and 10 thousand less than a given number.
I can find 100 thousand more and 10 thousand less than a given number.
I can find 10 million more and 10 million less than a given number.
I can find 100 million more and 100 million less than a given number.

weeks.title: Q1: W3 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to round multi-digit numbers to the thousands place using the vertical number line.
sc: I can use a vertical number line to round four-digit numbers to the nearest thousand.
I can use a vertical number line to round five- and six-digit numbers to the nearest thousand.

days.lo: I am learning to round multi-digit numbers to any place using the vertical number line.
sc: I can use a vertical number line to round five- and six-digit numbers to the nearest ten thousand.
I can use a vertical number line to round six-digit numbers to the nearest hundred thousand.
I can use estimation with addition and subtraction.

days.lo: I am learning to use place value understanding to round multi-digit numbers to any place value.
sc: I can round to the nearest thousand without using a number line.
I can round to the nearest ten thousand or hundred thousand without using a vertical line.
I can round to any value without using a number line.

days.lo: I am learning to use place value understanding to round multi-digit numbers to any place value using real-world applications.
sc: I can round one number to multiple units.
I can determine the best estimate to solve a word problem.
I can choose a unit of rounding to solve a word problem.

days.lo: I am learning to add multi-digit whole numbers and solve word problems using strip diagrams.
sc: I can add, renaming once, using place value disks in a place value chart.
I can add, renaming in multiple units, using the standard algorithm and the place value chart.
I can add, renaming multiple units using the standard algorithm.
I can solve a one-step word problem using the standard algorithm modeled with a strip diagram.

weeks.title: Q1: W4 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27 2

days.lo: I am learning to solve multi-step addition word problems modeled with strip diagrams, and assess the reasonableness of answers using rounding.
sc: I can solve a multi-step word problem using a strip diagram.
I can solve a two-step word problem using a strip problem and assess the reasonableness of the answer.
I can solve a multi-step word problem using a strip diagram and determine reasonableness.

days.lo: I am learning to use the standard algorithm to subtract, and solve word problems using strip diagrams.
sc: I can use a place value chart and place value disks to model subtracting alongside the algorithm, regrouping 1 hundred into 10 tens.
I can regroup 1 thousand into 10 hundreds using the subtraction algorithm.
Solve a subtraction word problem, regrouping 1 ten thousand into 10 thousands.

days.lo: I am learning to subtract, using the standard algorithm, and solve word problems using strip diagrams.
sc: I can subtract when I need to decompose twice.
I can subtract when I need to decompose three times.
I can use the subtraction algorithm to solve a word problem, modeled with a strip diagram, decomposing units 3 times.

days.lo: I am learning to solve two-step subtraction word problems modeled with strip diagrams and use rounding to assess reasonableness.
sc: I can solve a two-step word problem modeled with a strip diagram and assess the reasonableness of the answer using rounding.
I can solve a two-step problem, compared with smaller, unknown word problems

weeks.title: Q1: W5 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to solve multi-step addition and subtraction, modeled with strip diagrams, and rounding to assess reasonableness.
sc: I can solve multi-step word problems requiring addition and/or subtraction, modeled with a strip diagram.
I can check the reasonableness of the answer using estimation.

days.lo: I am learning to model and solve metric length word problems using addition and subtraction.
sc: I can understand 1 centimeter, 1 meter, and 1 kilometer in terms of concrete objects.
I can compare the sizes and note the relationships between meters and kilometers as conversion equivalencies.
I can add mixed units of length using the algorithm or simplifying strategies.
I can subtract mixed units of length using the algorithm or simplifying strategies.

days.lo: I am learning to model and solve metric mass word problems using addition and subtraction.
sc: I can convert kilograms to grams.
I can add mixed units of mass using the algorithm or a simplifying strategy.
I can subtract mixed units of mass using the algorithm or a simplifying strategy.
I can solve a word problem involving mixed units of mass, modeled with a strip diagram.

days.lo: I am learning to model and solve metric capacity word problems using addition and subtraction.
sc: I can compare the sizes and note the relationship between 1 liter and 1 milliliter.
I can add mixed units of capacity using the algorithm or a simplifying strategy.
I can subtract mixed units of capacity using the algorithm or a simplifying strategy.
I can solve a word problem involving mixed units of capacity.

weeks.title: Q1: W6 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to know and relate metric units to place value units in order to express measurements in different units.
sc: I can note the patterns of “times as much as” among units of length, mass, capacity, and place value.
I can relate units of length, mass, and capacity to units of place value.
I can compare metric units using place value knowledge and a number line.

days.lo: I am learning to solve multi-step word problems involving length, mass, and capacity.
sc: I can model the problem.
I can calculate to solve and write a statement.
I can assess the solution for reasonableness.

days.lo: I am learning to use the formulas for area and perimeter of rectangles.
sc: I can use formulas to solve for missing sides and compare the perimeter and area of a rectangle.
I can find all possible side combinations for a given area and their perimeters of rectangles.

days.lo: I am learning to solve multiplicative comparison word problems using the area and perimeter formulas.
sc: I can model a rectangle when given one side and use the interpret statement “times as” to find the missing side.
I can solve a multiplicative comparison word problem using the area and perimeter formulas.
I can observe the relationship of area and perimeter while solving a multiplicative word problem using the area and perimeter formulas.

days.lo: I am learning to demonstrate understanding of area and perimeter formulas by solving multi-step real-world problems.
sc: I can find all possible side lengths of a rectangle for a given area and use them to find the perimeter.
I can write an algebraic equation using a variable to stand for an unknown number.

weeks.title: Q1: W7 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning to interpret and represent patterns when multiplying by 10, 100, and 1,000 in arrays and numerically.
sc: I can draw place value disks to represent products when multiplying by a one-digit and two-digit number.
I can decompose multiples of 10 before multiplying.

days.lo: I am learning to interpret and represent patterns when multiplying by 10, 100, and 1,000 in arrays and numerically.
sc: I can use place value disks to represent multiplication patterns.
I can numerically represent single-digit numbers times a multiple of 10.
I can solve a word problem by finding the sum of two different products of a single-digit number by a two- and three-digit multiple of 10 and involving 1,000 times as many.

days.lo: I am learning to multiply two-digit multiples of 10 by two-digit multiples of 10 with the area model.
sc: I can use the place value chart to multiply a two-digit multiple of 10 by a two-digit multiple of 10.
I can create and use an area model to represent the multiplication of a two-digit multiple of 10 by a two-digit multiple of 10.

days.lo: I am learning how to use place value disks to represent two-digit by one-digit multiplication.
sc: I can represent a multiplication problem with disks.
I can write a matching equation for the model.
I can record the partial products vertically.

weeks.title: Q1: W8 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to use place value disks to represent three- and four- digit by one-digit multiplication.
sc: I can represent multiplication with disks, write a matching equation, and record the partial products vertically.
I can model and solve multiplication problems using a place value chart.
I can solve multiplication problems using a partial products drawing on a place value chart.

days.lo: I am learning how to multiply three- and four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers applying the standard algorithm.
sc: I can represent and solve multiplication in the place value chart and relate the process to solving using the standard algorithm.
I can solve multiplication using the partial products algorithm, solve using the standard algorithm, and relate the two methods to each other.
I can multiply three- and four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers applying the standard algorithm.

days.lo: I am learning how to connect the area model and the partial products method to the standard algorithm.
sc: I can multiply a three-digit number by a one-digit number using the area model.
I can multiply a three-digit number by a one-digit number, connecting the area model to the standard algorithm.
I can solve a word problem using the standard algorithm, area model, or partial products strategy.

days.lo: I am learning how to solve two-step word problems, including multiplicative comparison.
sc: I can model the problem.
I can calculate to solve and write a statement.
I can assess the solution.

days.lo: I am learning how to use multiplication, addition, or subtraction to solve multi-step word problems.
sc: I can model the problem.
I can calculate to solve and write a statement.
I can assess the solution.

weeks.title: Q1: W9 IPC Gr4 Eureka Math 26-27

days.lo: I am learning how to solve division word problems with remainders.
sc: I can divide a two-digit number by a one-digit number modeled with an array.
I can divide a two-digit number by a one-digit number with a remainder modeled with an array.
I can divide a two-digit number by a one-digit number with a remainder modeled with a strip diagram.
I can divide a two-digit number by a one-digit number, interpreting the remainder.
